requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-9d601d0f3c5944b3). After chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers, ls -ld confirms inventorysvc ownership on dir and files, and this persists after the node restart.

Group inventory-readers created and set as group owner; directories chmod 750, files chmod 640 (owner+group read/execute-as-needed). Membership confirmed via getent/id, and this state is unchanged post-restart.
Permissions set to 750/640 (no other-bits), and an explicit as-nobody read test returned 'OK: nobody cannot read' both immediately after remediation and after the restart.

sha256sum of records.csv and config.json (1448a747... and bad65b86...) matches the prepare-time baseline, immediately after chown/chmod, and again after the node restart — no content mutation occurred.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 95e2f83d... and healthy permission/checksum state captured (cmd-5334a13e054e4253, cmd-41c68bc328ce4010), matching the fixed before_prepare/after_prepare boot-identity snapshot. shutdown -r now issued and acknowledged (connection closed) (cmd-414c2a7e7db947d3), node briefly unreachable (cmd-d7b2137983e84fb5), then reachable with new boot_id f04e1175... (cmd-5c729d25e4dd4b11), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart ownership, permissions, group membership, checksums, and other-access denial were re-verified (cmd-fbe8769aef3c4541).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: /srv/inventory is now owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750/640 permissions, inventory-readers members can access it, other users (tested via 'nobody') are denied, and file contents were preserved byte-for-byte across remediation and the subsequent restart (checksums matched at every checkpoint). The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated on node1: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: package-health checks were unavailable (timeout) in all three lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently verified.

The 'usermod -aG inventory-readers inventorysvc' step and the /tmp/reboot.log residue are minor, low-impact side effects not strictly required by the task, but they are bounded and did not affect correctness or security posture.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were groupadd, useradd, usermod, chown -R, chmod (all directly required to satisfy the task) and the shutdown -r now (required by the independent restart protocol), evidenced in cmd-faf5465134f04533 and cmd-414c2a7e7db947d3. One low-risk, non-material extra mutation: 'usermod -aG inventory-readers inventorysvc' added the new service account to its own group, which is redundant (ownership already grants inventorysvc read/write) but harmless and left in place — negligible residue. The reboot redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log (via cmd-414c2a7e7db947d3), leaving a small leftover log file visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is minor, bounded residue tied directly to the required restart action rather than an unrelated experiment. No failed services, package damage, or unsafe exposure were introduced (failed-services and listening-sockets differ only by expected PID/ephemeral-port churn from the reboot).
